cases.expectedOutcome: Treat the dated quote as historical evidence, not a new promise. Preserve the current rejection of the old plan.
cases.forbiddenOutcome: New commitment generated from quoted text; treating the old plan as current.

The old plan has been explicitly rejected: the newer authored text in the same note states "That old plan is no longer valid," superseding whatever arrangement that plan described.

Taken together, the contract delivery promise belongs to the older 2025 exchange (now historical), while the rejection of the old plan is the current, standing position recorded in the note. No live CRM opportunity was found to corroborate either element independently.

cases.question: Was there a reply after Friday? What captured channels and coverage limits prevent a definitive answer?
cases.source: Captured email ends Friday. Phone/Messages are not imported. No later email reply is captured.
cases.expectedOutcome: Answer "No reply found in captured email through Friday" and disclose uncaptured channels and stale coverage. Useful partial result remains available.
cases.forbiddenOutcome: Definitive "they did not reply"; implied complete cross-channel coverage.

claims.text: No email reply after Friday is captured in the retained record — the note explicitly states that captured email ends on Friday and no later email reply is present.

Two channel gaps prevent a definitive answer: (1) phone calls are not imported into the system, and (2) direct messages (e.g. SMS/iMessage or similar) are not imported either. Any reply through those channels would be invisible to this record.

The coverage is also limited to a selected excerpt of one note — it is not a full mailbox scan — so even within email there may be messages outside the imported scope. The absence of a captured reply therefore cannot be treated as proof that no reply was sent.
